result.summary:
Read TEST-DESIGNER's handoff (handoffs/WF03-ISS0782-20260923/step-04-test-designer.json) in full, plus the actual test files and test/specs/ISS-0782.md directly.

COVERAGE CHECK: web/src/api/__tests__/identity.usersRoles.test.ts has one test per each of the 5 call sites ISS-0782 lists as affected -- usersApi.list (GET /api/v1/identity/users), usersApi.get (GET /api/v1/identity/users/:id), usersApi.create (POST /api/v1/identity/users), usersApi.update (PATCH /api/v1/identity/users/:id), rolesApi.list (GET /api/v1/identity/roles). Cross-checked against `git show 2e36f8c2 -- web/src/api/identity.ts`: exactly these 5 call sites changed in the fix commit, and all 5 are covered -- no gap, no extra untested site silently left uncovered from the fix's own diff. Confirmed no @tag :skip and no TODO/implement placeholder (grep for 'skip'/'TODO' in the file: no matches).

ASSERTION QUALITY: each test asserts BOTH the correct path via `toContain` AND explicitly rules out the specific wrong pre-fix literal via `not.toContain`/`not.toMatch` (e.g. usersApi.list also excludes `/api/v1/users(\?|$)` via regex, not just a substring check that could pass on both old and new paths since '/api/v1/users' is a substring of '/api/v1/identity/users'... actually verified this matters: '/api/v1/identity/users' does NOT contain the literal '/api/v1/users' as a prefix-anchored path, but the regex negative check specifically guards against the old bare route pattern with a word/query boundary, which is a correct, deliberate design against a false-pass on substring containment). Method assertions (POST/PATCH) also checked via `objectContaining`. This is discriminating -- a reintroduced wrong-path regression would fail these tests, not just a missing-call regression.

INDEPENDENT FAIL-SIDE REPRODUCTION (own throwaway worktree, not TEST-DESIGNER's): confirmed `git rev-parse 2e36f8c2^` == `a1cb9604` (matches TEST-DESIGNER's claimed pre-fix commit). Created `git worktree add --detach ../letflow-tdv-iss0782-prefix a1cb9604` myself. Verified before running that the worktree's web/src/api/identity.ts still had the pre-fix literals (grep confirmed: '/api/v1/users', '/api/v1/admin/roles' etc., no '/api/v1/identity/users' or '/api/v1/identity/roles' present). Copied ONLY web/src/api/__tests__/identity.usersRoles.test.ts into that worktree (nothing else from the branch), junctioned node_modules from the main checkout via `mklink /J` to avoid a redundant npm install. Ran `npx vitest run src/api/__tests__/identity.usersRoles.test.ts` there. Real output: 5 failed / 5, each on the exact literal TEST-DESIGNER reported --
  usersApi.list:   expected '/api/v1/users/u-1' style mismatch -> 'expected /api/v1/users?search=foo to contain /api/v1/identity/users' (observed as separate assertion failures per test, matching)
  usersApi.get:    AssertionError: expected '/api/v1/users/u-1' to contain '/api/v1/identity/users/u-1'
  usersApi.create: AssertionError: expected '/api/v1/admin/users' to contain '/api/v1/identity/users'
  usersApi.update: AssertionError: expected '/api/v1/users/u-3' to contain '/api/v1/identity/users/u-3'
  rolesApi.list:   AssertionError: expected '/api/v1/admin/roles' to contain '/api/v1/identity/roles'
  Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 5 failed (5)
This matches TEST-DESIGNER's claimed output exactly (same 5 failures, same literals) -- independently confirmed, not copied. Removed the node_modules junction (`cmd /c rmdir node_modules`) then `git worktree remove --force ../letflow-tdv-iss0782-prefix`; `git worktree list` on the main checkout no longer shows it, and `ls ../letflow-tdv-iss0782-prefix` confirms the directory is gone.

INDEPENDENT PASS-SIDE REPRODUCTION (this branch, post-fix): ran `npx vitest run src/api/__tests__/identity.usersRoles.test.ts` in web/ on this checkout. Real output: 'Test Files 1 passed (1)' / 'Tests 5 passed (5)' in 8ms.

GIT STATE VERIFICATION: `git status --porcelain` on the main checkout after all of the above shows only the pre-existing, unrelated untracked `web/tests/e2e/.pipeline-state/` directory (present before this gate started, not touched by it) -- no leftover mutation from the worktree work, which touched only the separate worktree directory and its own node_modules junction, both now removed.

LIVE-E2E LEVEL: did NOT independently re-run. `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq erl.exe"` confirmed no backend process running in this shared, non-worktree primary checkout before I started. Re-running TEST-DESIGNER's live e2e fail-then-pass proof would require starting the backend (mix run --no-halt) against the shared letflow-postgres-1/letflow-keycloak-1 containers and temporarily overwriting web/src/api/identity.ts in place in this SAME shared checkout other agents/sessions may be using concurrently -- a materially different risk profile from the mocked-level worktree reproduction, which never touches the shared checkout at all. Per this run's own instructions, I am skipping this independent re-run and relying on the workflow doc's own stated rule: the mandatory mutant-reproduction bar in WF-03 Step 4's "non-existence" carve-out applies to a fix that ADDS a module (pre-fix failure = UndefinedFunctionError, proving nothing about discrimination). ISS-0782 is the opposite case: it fixes EXISTING behavior (wrong path literals in an existing module) where the pre-fix failure is a real, path-specific assertion mismatch, not a not-found error -- so the mocked-level fail-then-pass I reproduced myself already IS a direct mutant-equivalent proof (the 'mutant' here is literally the real pre-fix code, and the failures are specific to the exact wrong literals, not a blanket not-found). The live e2e level is corroborating evidence on top of that, not the load-bearing proof, and TEST-DESIGNER's own handoff/test/specs/ISS-0782.md already documents why: 'this is why test asset (1), the mocked unit test, is this run's fully-green fail-then-pass proof.' I accept that framing rather than re-deriving the live-e2e result myself, given the shared-checkout risk.

ISSUES ARRAY CHECK: TEST-DESIGNER's handoff `result.issues` DOES contain an explicit entry flagging the pre-existing 403/permission-provisioning gap in the shared dev Keycloak realm as a separate, out-of-scope concern warranting its own issue -- not silently omitted. test/specs/ISS-0782.md's "Fail-then-pass proof" section corroborates this with the backend's own log line (`sync_role_claims_from_token/3: zero group_ids resolved...`) and ISSUE-FIXER's Step 1 diagnosis (curl showing 403, not 404, on the corrected routes). This is reasonable to accept as documented and out-of-scope rather than a coverage gap in THIS issue's test design: ISS-0782's own scope (per its title/description/suggested_fix) is the routing-literal defect only, which the mocked test proves fixed with a fully-green result; the 403 is a distinct, already-diagnosed authorization/grant-provisioning defect in the dev environment's realm seed data, unrelated to identity.ts's path literals, and correctly not papered over by loosening the live e2e assertion.

No shared hardcoded state dependency in the new mocked test (each test builds its own fetchSpy via vi.fn(), beforeEach/afterEach reset token and restore mocks). Tests are self-sufficient -- no ordering dependency between the 5 `it` blocks. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in either test file.

All acceptance criteria met. Gate: PASS.
